text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim said it had temporarily suspended the production of jet fuel due to technological reasons.
-- Bulgaria's state commercial fleet said it had posted 7.9 billion levs net profit for last year. @

-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it had withdrawn its insolvency bid against private Mollov bank and had lifted the receivership from the bank because Mollov bank's financial state had improved thanks to a $6.25 million investment by the Slovak investment fund Istrocapital in March.

-- Bulgarian customs officers at the Bulgarian-Yugoslav border checkpoint Kalotina said they had seized 1,278 pirate CD's worth 12.8 million levs and hidden in a Bulgarian passenger bus owned by the private Vitosha Express company and travelling to Yugoslavia.
-- Bulgaria will not become eligible for a NATO membership in the next 10 years because of social and economic reasons, former Socialist Prime minister Zhan Videnov said.

-- The Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) would walk out of the President's Consultative Council for National Security because of unjustified management reshuffles at state enterprises and the high social price of structural reforms implemented by the interim cabinet, BSP leader Georgi Parvanov said.

-- The Mausoleum in central Sofia which once housed the embalmed body of Bulgaria's first communist leader Georgi Dimitrov was covered with more than 100 dalmation spots as a part of a promotion of Disney's classic "101 Dalmations" live-action re-make.
-- Bulgaria's interim government is expected to raise salaries in the public sector by 35 percent from May 1, Social care minister Ivan Neikov said.
